newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African firm in talks on satellite launches.
newsitem.headline: S.African firm in talks on satellite launches.

text.p: A division of South African arms maker Denel said on Monday it was negotiating with several foreign companies to provide launch facilities for rockets carrying satellites into low-Earth orbit.
"We are having discussions with various groups of people and there is a real interest in using the facilities in South Africa," Ian Farr, divisional manager of Houwteq, told Reuters.

"If things go according to plan and if the negotiations are pulled off, we will integrate satellites at the Houwteq facilites and we will use the launch facility at Overberg, to launch satellites into low-earth orbit," he said.

The Overberg site, near Bredasdorp 160 km southeast of Cape Town, was developed by the previous apartheid government as part of a military rocket programme. The programme was aborted after pressure from the U.S.
Farr said Houwteq was keen to see better use made of the Overberg facilities.
"We expect at least a couple of launches a year... We hope by the end of the year we'll know where we stand."
He said contracts under discussion could result in foreign currency revenue of up to 500 million rand ($107 million) a year.
"We will bring launch vehicles in from outside, we will do final preparation here, and launch them," Farr said.
